title: 2x4 Captured-Post Sawhorses (Set of 2)
summary: A pair of heavy-duty 30" sawhorses built from six 2x4s, with a channeled double-rail top and crossed A-frame legs.
description: A pair of stout 2x4 sawhorses: 30" tall with a 36" x 4 1/2" top and a 23" footprint. The top is two 2x4s on edge with a 1 1/2" channel between them, and at each end a vertical post drops into that channel and is screwed through both rails. Two legs cross the post, one on each face, in an X. Their square-to-the-floor tops bear right under the rails, so weight on the top goes straight down the legs and doesn't rest on the screws. A flat stretcher low on each end frame ties the legs together and carries the post. Every joint is a glued, screwed butt joint, and the only angle cut is a 20° miter at each end of the legs.

tools.note: Must miter to 20°. A circular saw and speed square also work.
Two clamps hold the rails to the posts while you drive screws.

materials.name: Board, 2x4 96"
materials.note: Buy full 96" boards, not 92 5/8" precut studs. The rail boards need about 92 7/8". Pick straight boards with no large knots in the 36" rail sections.

cutList.note: Square both ends. Two per sawhorse, set on edge.
20° miter on both ends, cuts parallel (a parallelogram). Measure 28 3/16" along either long edge.
Square both ends. One per end frame.
Square both ends. One per end frame, laid flat.

steps.title: Cut the parts
steps.body:
Cut the parts from six 8' 2x4s laid out like this so nothing runs short:
Boards 1 and 2: two 36" top rails + one 20 1/2" post.
Boards 3 and 4: three legs each.
Board 5: two legs + one 20 1/2" post.
Board 6: one 20 1/2" post + four 16 1/2" stretchers.
Legs: set the miter saw to 20° and trim the end of the board. Measure 28 3/16" along the edge and cut again at 20° in the SAME direction, so the two cuts are parallel. The next leg starts from that cut, so three legs fit on one board with only a small wedge of waste. Make all eight legs identical; the X comes from flipping them at assembly.

steps.title: Mark the posts and legs
steps.body:
On every post, square a line around all four faces 3 1/2" down from one end. This is the rail line: the part above it sits inside the top channel, and the leg tops butt against it.
On the top (short) cut of each leg, mark the center, 1 7/8" from either corner along the cut.
On every stretcher, mark the center of its length (8 1/4").

steps.title: Set up the end frame
steps.body: Each sawhorse has two end frames, so you will build four. On a flat bench, stand a post and a stretcher on their narrow edges so their 3 1/2" sides are vertical and their top faces are level with each other. Butt the bottom end of the post (the end away from the rail line) against the wide 3 1/2" face of the stretcher, centered on the stretcher's center mark, and make it square. Glue the joint and drive two 3" screws through the stretcher into the end of the post.

steps.title: Attach the first leg
steps.body: Lay a leg across the post and stretcher, angled out to the left. Line up its top cut with the post's rail line and its top center mark with the center of the post. The angle sets itself: when the top cut is parallel to the stretcher, the leg is at 20°. Check with a speed square. The foot should end 8" past the stretcher's lower edge. Glue the contact areas, then drive two 3" screws through the leg into the post (stay on the post's centerline, 1" and 3" below the rail line) and two 3" screws through the leg into the stretcher. The stretcher end can stand slightly proud of the leg's outer edge. Leave it or plane it flush.

steps.title: Attach the crossing leg
steps.body: Flip the frame over. Lay a second leg on this face so its foot lands at the OPPOSITE end of the stretcher from the first leg's foot. Flip the leg over if its cuts won't sit parallel to the stretcher. Set it the same way: top cut on the rail line, centered on the post, parallel to the stretcher. The two legs now cross in an X just below the rail line. Glue and screw it the same way, two 3" screws into the post and two into the stretcher. These post screws can't hit the first leg's screws: each goes only 1 1/2" into the 3 1/2" post. Check that both feet sit flat on the same line about 23" apart outside-to-outside. Build the other three end frames the same way.

steps.title: Mark the rails
steps.body: On the inside face of each top rail, mark 3" and 6 1/2" in from each end. Each post sits between these marks, leaving 3" of rail overhanging the post and 1 1/2" overhanging the outer leg.

steps.title: Assemble the top upside down
steps.body: Assemble upside down on a flat floor. That makes the rail tops and post tops flush with no measuring. Lay two rails on edge, upside down, 1 1/2" apart (a scrap of 2x4 laid flat is the spacer). Glue the top 3 1/2" of each post on both wide faces. Drop two end frames upside down into the channel at the rail marks so the post tops touch the floor. The leg tops will land on the rail edges at the same moment. Clamp the rails to the posts. Drive two 2 1/2" screws through each rail into each post, offset from the screws on the other side. That is eight per sawhorse.

steps.title: Check and finish
steps.body: Flip the sawhorse onto its feet on the flat floor. If it rocks, mark the long foot and trim it a little at a time. Repeat the top assembly for the second sawhorse. Ease the sharp edges with sandpaper if you like. The 1 1/2" channel in the top can hold a sacrificial 2x2 or a clamp bar. Let the glue cure overnight before heavy use.
